page.title: Best low profile mechanical keyboard for Mac (2026): Lofree Flow 2 vs Keychron K3 Max vs NuPhy Air75 V3
page.h1: Best low profile mechanical keyboard for Mac
page.desc: Lofree Flow 2 84 for Mac wins on build and typing feel; Keychron K3 Max wins on price and remapping. Owner complaints, specs and prices checked 2026-11-06.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best low profile mechanical keyboard for Mac is the Lofree Flow 2 84 for Mac ({buy:lofree-flow-2-84-for-mac}): a CNC-machined aluminum board (about 745 g, 21.5 mm tall) with a macOS-default layout, a 3,000 mAh battery rated 90 to 120 hours with the backlight off, and three ways to connect: USB-C, Bluetooth 5.3, or a 1,000 Hz 2.4 GHz dongle. The biggest complaint about Lofree boards is Bluetooth: the original Flow took 2 to 5 seconds to wake and had no dongle. The Flow 2 fixes that with the included 2.4 GHz receiver, so use the dongle on the Mac and keep Bluetooth for an iPad. If you want in-browser remapping without emailing support, or want to stay under $100, the Keychron K3 Max wins at $89.99 (keychron.com, 2026-11-06). If battery life matters most, the NuPhy Air75 V3's 4,000 mAh cell is rated 1,200 hours with lighting off.

The Flow 2 for Mac comes only with Surfer linear switches. If you want a tactile bump, buy the standard Flow 2 84 in Space Gray ({buy:lofree-flow-2-84}), which uses Pulse tactile switches; the Silver Void version is the silent one for shared offices. Both are the same aluminum body, battery and wireless hardware. The Lofree store had a "Black Friday Month, keyboards 20% off" banner on 2026-11-06 with no code; the prices above already reflect it.

Two things to know before you buy any Flow 2. Remapping works through VIA, but the keyboard is not in VIA's database, so you must load a JSON file that Lofree sends on request. And the touch strip on the right edge changes volume when a palm brushes it; holding Fn + Space for three seconds turns it off.

page.after:
What owners and reviewers complain about

  • Bluetooth wake and dropouts (6 sources). The original Flow takes 2 to 5 seconds to reconnect after sleep, and several reviewers switched to USB. Flow 2 owners report the same deep-sleep pause and occasional macOS dropouts on Bluetooth; the 2.4 GHz dongle is the fix, and it is in the box.
  • VIA setup (5 sources). VIA recognizes the Flow 2 but will not connect until you load Lofree's JSON definition, which is not on the website. Email support for it before you need it.
  • Touch strip (5 sources). It changes volume or brightness when brushed, cannot be remapped, and the strip plus side USB-C port push your mouse about 3 cm to the right.
  • Battery with backlight on (4 sources). Basic Tutorials measured 21 hours at full brightness; PCWorld lost 20% in three days over Bluetooth. Lights off, reviewers got 80 hours or more.
  • Cramped 100-key layout (3 sources). The Flow 2 100 squeezes the numpad against the arrow keys. Reviewers who tested it recommend the 84.
  • Sound (1 source). Tom's Guide called the stabilizers and case acoustics poor; Digital Trends, 9to5Toys and Basic Tutorials did not hear it.

Which one, by need

  • Best typing feel and build on a Mac: Lofree Flow 2 84 for Mac. Aluminum body, Mac-default keys, dongle included. Choose the standard Flow 2 84 in Space Gray if you want a tactile switch.
  • Best value and easiest remapping: Keychron K3 Max. QMK/VIA works in the browser with no file, both keycap sets come in the box, and it is under $100. Plastic body and a 1,550 mAh battery are the trade-offs.
  • Longest battery or more key travel: NuPhy Air75 V3. 4,000 mAh cell and 3.5 mm travel switches, with an aluminum top and plastic bottom.
  • Office board that pairs with three devices and never needs software: Logitech MX Mechanical Mini for Mac, but it is Bluetooth only and the switches are soldered.

Not recommended

  • Lofree Flow 2 100 if you type numbers: three reviewers found the numpad placement caused wrong entries.
  • Original Lofree Flow84 for wireless use. It is a fine wired desk board at $119, but Bluetooth-only wireless with a 2 to 5 second wake delay and no remapping is why the Flow 2 exists.
  • Logitech MX Mechanical Mini for Mac as a typing upgrade: Voltcave rated its typing feel poor, switches cannot be changed, and it costs more than the Lofree.
